description: This case study is a REACH Initiative assessment, posted on ReliefWeb on 18 September 2024, of the needs and damages of Ukraine's district heating sector ahead of the 2024/2025 winter. Key findings from the surveyed facilities: 24 facilities across ten oblasts reported damage to heat production, 18 across nine oblasts damage to distribution networks, 18 insufficient capacity, 74 the need for rehabilitation, and 66% of 97 companies too little money to keep running, with backup generators, boilers and cogeneration units the main requests. It puts war damage to the sector at 2.1 billion US dollars and losses at 2.3 billion by December 2023 and counts 53 attacks on thermal power, heating and water facilities between January and June 2024, mapped by oblast. Access: free PDF download from ReliefWeb; no licence is stated beyond the site terms. Coverage is Ukraine's district heating companies in the surveyed oblasts. Caveats: only the ReliefWeb summary was read, not the PDF, and the findings are survey reports by companies. It suits recovery, resilience and emergency response studies of district heating under attack, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Winter Heating Crisis: An Assessment of Ukraine's District Heating Needs and Damages (REACH Initiative, July 2024)
outcomes: Among the district heating facilities surveyed, 24 across ten oblasts reported damage to heat production and 18 across nine oblasts damage to distribution networks, 18 reported insufficient capacity, 74 needed rehabilitation, and 66% of the 97 companies assessed lacked funds to keep operating. Companies asked for backup generators, boilers and cogeneration units, and nearly half reported staffing shortages. War damage to the sector was estimated at 2.1 billion US dollars with 2.3 billion of losses by December 2023.
